rationale: All three lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran with parseable output; every acceptance criterion of EPMCDME-15739 and EPMCDME-15747 passes. Three defects introduced by the change block: the in-place refresh leaves the panel editable, so a role, user-type or budget save can be repainted by an older refresh snapshot; the role save writes from a stale closure; and the 25% Role column can be narrower than its fixed 192px select below the lg breakpoint. 4 findings deferred as pre-existing (a mutation finishing after the popup was closed or reopened for another user, failed budget refetch clearing assignments, double-clicking a confirm button, swallowed unassign error); 14 dismissed (the updater and refresh ordering already matches the existing set-default path, the table has a single consumer, the initial load keeps its spinner, other edit handlers never refetched).

findings.title: Role select overflows the narrower column
findings.problem: The Role column dropped to 25% while its select keeps a fixed 192px width; the table is table-fixed and the popup goes full width below the lg breakpoint.
findings.impact: On narrow screens the select spills into the actions column, breaking AC3 (no overlap, controls usable).
findings.recommendation: Make the select fluid up to its current width (w-full max-w-48).

findings.title: Save during in-place refresh gets repainted
findings.problem: The post-project-change refresh no longer blocks the panel, so a role, user-type or budget save can complete while that refresh is reading the pre-save snapshot; the refresh then overwrites roleFlags, userType and budgets with old values.
findings.impact: Controls show the old value after a successful save, with nothing to correct it.
findings.recommendation: On save success re-apply the confirmed value and, if a refresh is in flight, start a newer refresh so the stale response is discarded.

findings.title: Role save writes user from stale closure
findings.problem: handleRoleChange sets setUser({ ...user, ...nextFlags }) with the user captured when the save started.
findings.impact: A project change or refresh that landed meanwhile is reverted in the table, and with the in-place refresh nothing re-corrects it.
findings.recommendation: Use the functional form: setUser((current) => (current ? { ...current, ...nextFlags } : current)).
